summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against every clause of the selected Greek working source. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both retain the distinctions between resentment, confession, mercy, repentance, and healing; the difficult assertion about living only with difficulty; and the conditional cleansing requirement and death consequence. The simplified edition’s sentence restructuring preserves the substance and speaker attribution. The notes appropriately distinguish editorial restorations from directly preserved letters and do not claim fresh manuscript collation. Reported alternatives concerning adjacent sections do not require changes to this selected section. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied working source and the accuracy of the supplied disclosures, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or scholarly certification.
